heading: Paramount settles with US states to clear $110bn Warner Bros Discovery deal, says report—Check conditions, penalties | Company Business News
paragraphs: Media giant Paramount Skydance has settled with 12 American states that sued to block its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, Reuters reported today, citing a source in the know.
The move clears the path for Paramount's hyped acquisition that would reshape Hollywood, the report added.
Both Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery did not immediately respond to queries from Reuters about the settlement offer, it said.
As per the report, the settlement requires that the following conditions be fulfilled:

The report noted that this settlement removes a major roadblock to Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros, which would essentially create one of the largest media mergers in history. It also allows Paramount to “unite” two of Hollywood's biggest film studios, two major streaming services and two of the largest cable-news operations under a single owner, it added.

Reuters was the first to report that Paramount and the states were expected to settle as soon as the weekend, with independent content monitoring of CNN and a commitment on the number of theatrical releases among the terms under discussion, the report added.

Later on, Sunday, 20 September, the Wall Street Journal reported that the two sides had discussed a number of stipulations, including a $1.5 billion investment in production in the state, a commitment not to sell either studio lot, and potential penalties if Paramount fails to honor a pledge to produce 30 movies a year after the merger.
Other measures under consideration include selling some cable channels and creating a board to help ensure CNN retains editorial independence, WSJ had reported.

While Trump administration regulators had cleared the multi-million merger deal, a coalition of 12 state attorneys general, led by California's Rob Bonta, sued in July to block the acquisition. They argued the merger would reduce competition and create a media behemoth with the power to raise prices in movies and television.
A settlement will help Paramount avoid a $7 million daily fee it owes Warner Bros shareholders for each day the deal does not close past September 30.
Notably, antitrust regulators in other jurisdictions globally, including the European Union (EU) and Britain, have already cleared the acquisition, the report added.

Explaining the settlement deal for the Paramount-Warner Brothers Discovery merger, New Jersey Attorney General said that under the settlement, the merger company will make annual contribution of $5 million per year, for a total of $25 million.
She added that the merged company will also commit to $47.5 million in workforce fund over five years; and has agreed to create editorial independence boards for CNN and CBS.
In a statement, Paramount said that having addressed the US state AGs and WGA's concerns, it now has complete clearance for the Warner Brothers Discovery deal.
